I've been farming this land in Quzhou for 5 years now. I know this county well — the soils here on the North China Plain are decent but water is always on my mind since I'm pulling from a well. With 220.1 mu split between millet and spring soybean, I need to be efficient with every input.

I'll split my land roughly in half. Soybean fixes its own nitrogen, so I keep fertilizer costs down on that side. For millet, I'll go with an improved variety — something adapted to our region that gives me better drought tolerance and yield than the old landraces my neighbors still use. My education helped me understand variety selection early on. I use rotary tillage across both crops since I don't have the depth of compaction issues that would justify ploughing, and it saves fuel costs.

Irrigation is my biggest constraint. I'll irrigate millet three times — at planting, jointing, and grain fill — and soybean three times as well at germination, flowering, and pod fill. I won't over-irrigate; well water costs money to pump. Two rounds of pesticide per crop is my standard — one early preventative and one reactive if I see pressure building.
